exact.проездной за какой-то давний месяц: a travel pass for some long-ago month
exact.Вот проездной, месяц уже не разобрать. Я: Here's a travel pass, you can't make out the month any more. I suppose I kept it because that month I crossed the whole city every day and was very proud of it.
exact.В Берлине перемены приходили то под земл: In Berlin changes came either underground or overhead: the U-Bahn, Tempelhof airfield, the radio tower. And then the city lived divided for so long that people asked each other which district first and how they were keeping only after.
exact.Однажды в воскресенье мы поехали за горо: One Sunday we went out of town to swim and left the bag of food at home. We ate nothing all day but the cherries we'd bought by the road, and we still argue about whose fault it was.
exact.Картонный кружок, на который ставят круж: A cardboard mat, the kind you put your beer on. There's somebody's phone number on the back, I can't remember whose, and I'm too scared to ring it.
exact.Мюнхен при мне всё время что-нибудь стро: Munich was always building something in my time: the BMW works, then the U-Bahn, then everything at once for the Olympics. At home we noticed the changes by how many newcomers there were and how much the flat had gone up.
exact.Как-то мы с соседкой решили сами перекле: Once my neighbour and I decided to re-paper the room ourselves, and by evening we'd hung it upside down. The little flowers were looking at the floor, we laughed and left it, and the guests never noticed.
exact.бумажный цветок с отклеившимся лепестком: a paper flower with a petal come unstuck
exact.Бумажный цветок, видишь, один лепесток о: A paper flower, see, one petal's come unstuck. Somebody pushed it into my hand in the street, and for forty years I haven't had the heart to throw it away.
exact.В Кёльне многое мерили Рейном: докуда по: In Cologne a lot of things were measured by the Rhine: how high the water rose, when they opened the cable car across the river, when the station opened again. After the war the city was rebuilt for so long that children thought scaffolding just grew on houses.
exact.Однажды я пекла пирог к соседскому дню р: Once I was baking a cake for a neighbour's birthday and only remembered it by the smell. We cut off the top, covered the rest in sugar, and afterwards the neighbour asked for the recipe.
exact.пропуск на ярмарку с загнутым углом: a fair pass with a bent corner
exact.Вот старый пропуск на ярмарку, угол загн: Here's an old pass for the fair, the corner's bent. A friend gave it to me, and that time I never went.
exact.Лейпциг жил ярмаркой и вокзалом, это был: Leipzig lived by its fair and its station, that was the main thing. Then they ran the S-Bahn to Halle and built Grünau, and the talk at home was about who'd been given a flat and how long it took to get anywhere now.
exact.Как-то зимой мы с подругой полдня просто: One winter my friend and I stood in a queue for half a day and only found out what we were queuing for at the counter. It turned out to be tangerines, and we carried them home like flowers.
exact.жетон с пароходной пристани: a copper token from a ferry pier
exact.Жетон с пристани, медный. Им давно нигде: A token from the pier, copper. You can't pay with it anywhere now, but I keep it in my coat pocket, it gets warm if you hold it long enough.
exact.В Гамбурге всё шло от порта и от Эльбы:: In Hamburg everything came from the port and the Elbe: the tunnel under the river, the U-Bahn, the newspapers they printed here. At home we learned about changes from the hooters on the water and from where you had to change trains now.
exact.Однажды в воскресенье ветер с Эльбы унёс: One Sunday the wind off the Elbe blew my hat straight into the water. Some lad fished it out with a stick, I gave him a coin, and I wore that hat for another ten years.
exact.ключ на кольце с пластмассовой биркой: a key on a ring with a plastic tag
exact.Ключ с пластмассовой биркой, номер кварт: A key with a plastic tag, the flat number's almost worn off. That flat hasn't been mine for ages, but the key stayed.
exact.Вокруг Галле всё вертелось вокруг химии:: Around Halle everything turned on chemistry: the works, the trains, a whole new town for the chemical workers. At home we talked about who was on which shift and who'd got a flat in Neustadt.
exact.Как-то летом мы всем двором собрались жа: One summer the whole block got together to grill sausages, and the coals just wouldn't catch. While we fussed it started to rain, and in the end we fried the sausages in a pan in my kitchen, ten of us.
exact.пуговица от рабочей куртки: a button from a work jacket
exact.Пуговица, большая, от рабочей куртки. Ку: A button, a big one, from a work jacket. The jacket went long ago, but the button keeps rolling round the drawer, and I know it every time.
exact.Наш городок на Одере сначала жил гаванью: Our little town on the Oder lived by the harbour and the river at first, and then the steelworks grew up next to it with a new town of its own. The names changed so much that I addressed letters one way and then another, and the postman brought them anyway.
exact.Однажды я решила сама подстричь чёлку пе: Once I decided to cut my own fringe before a dance and cut it so badly I had to wear a headscarf. My friend said that was the fashion now, and the next week she turned up in a headscarf herself.
exact.входной билет с оторванным корешком: an entrance ticket with the stub torn off
A ticket for the play, the stub's torn off. I sat somewhere you mostly saw other people's hats, but I keep the ticket.
exact.У нас в деревне время считали десятилети: In our village time was counted in decades, from one Passion Play to the next. In between we lived quietly, and in a play year every house worked out how many rooms it could let and where to sleep itself.
exact.Однажды зимой корова соседей ушла по сне: One winter the neighbours' cow wandered across the snow into our yard and wouldn't leave. We spent half the day coaxing her with bread, and she chose our cabbages instead.
exact.спичечный коробок с семенами: a matchbox with seeds in it
exact.Коробок, а в нём семена. Подписано моей: A matchbox, and seeds inside. It's labelled in my own hand, but I can't read what the seeds are any more, so I don't dare plant them.
exact.В Альтмарке перемены приходили медленно,: In the Altmark changes came slowly and then all at once: the cooperative, the gas rigs, the power station near Stendal that was never finished. At home we talked more about the line: was the train still running, and how far.
exact.Как-то на сенокосе мы с подругой сели пе: Once at haymaking my friend and I sat down in the shade for a breather and slept half the day. They found us by the snoring, and we're still arguing about which of us it was.
exact.продавщица в универмаге KaDeWe в Берлине: saleswoman at the KaDeWe department store in Berlin
exact.Меня взяли в KaDeWe, в отдел чулок. Перв: They took me on at KaDeWe, in stockings. The first week I looked at the customers more than I sold to them, and the senior saleswoman called me "our sightseer".
exact.Постоянных покупательниц я знала по голо: I knew the regular customers by their voices and their shoe size. Sometimes I thought I knew more about half of Berlin than their husbands did.
exact.Из универмага я ушла давно, а привычка с: I left the store long ago, but the habit of folding everything into neat piles stayed. The towels in my cupboard lie as if someone's about to buy them.
exact.работница на заводе BMW в Мюнхене: worker at the BMW works in Munich
exact.Я пошла на BMW, на сборку. В первый день: I went to BMW, on assembly. On the first day the foreman showed me one operation and said that was all I needed to know, and I was offended for a week.
exact.Со временем я знала не одну операцию, а: In time I knew not one operation but five, and the foreman admitted it. Not in words, of course, but by putting the new girls next to me.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с BMW. Когда по улице п: I retired from BMW. When one of their cars goes by I still look to see if the door sits straight.
exact.секретарша в редакции в Гамбурге: secretary at a newspaper office in Hamburg
exact.После курсов стенографии меня взяли секр: After a shorthand course they took me on as a secretary at a newspaper. Everyone smoked, everyone rushed, and everyone thought their article mattered more than the rest and that I should type it.
exact.Я научилась отвечать по телефону так, чт: I learned to answer the phone so that nobody could tell whether the editor was in or not. That was my main skill, I reckon.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из редакции. Газету до: I retired from the newspaper. I still read the paper with a pencil and find misprints, though nobody asks me to any more.
exact.конторщица Лейпцигской ярмарки: clerk at the Leipzig fair office
exact.После курсов счетоводства я пошла в конт: After a book-keeping course I went into the fair office. All year it was quiet there, and two weeks before the opening it got so bad I only came home to sleep.
exact.Я знала, какая фирма где стоит, лучше, ч: I knew which firm stood where better than the firms did. People stopped me in the corridor like an information desk, and I never once said it wasn't my job.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из конторы ярмарки. Ког: I retired from the fair office. When the radio talks about a big exhibition my mood still drops, as if it's all about to land on me again.
exact.работница на заводе Volkswagen в Вольфсб: worker at the Volkswagen works in Wolfsburg
exact.Я пошла на Volkswagen, в цех, где обтяги: I went to Volkswagen, to the shop where they covered the seats. The town then was such that apart from the works there was hardly anything to talk about, so we talked about the works.
exact.Рядом со мной в разное время работали лю: Over the years people from all over worked next to me, and I learned a few words in three languages. Mostly they were words about lunch.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с завода. «Жука» на ули: I retired from the works. I still follow a Beetle in the street with my eyes, like an old acquaintance.
exact.работница на металлургическом комбинате: worker at the EKO steelworks in Eisenhüttenstadt
exact.Меня взяли на комбинат, в лабораторию пр: They took me on at the steelworks, in the laboratory by the furnaces, carrying samples. The first week I was afraid of dropping a sample, then I realised it was the furnace I should be afraid of, and it got easier.
exact.Город строился вокруг нас, и каждый год: The town was built around us, and every year a new block went up. I used to laugh that the works grew faster than the neighbours' children, and the neighbours said faster than the wages.
exact.С комбината я в конце концов ушла. По ут: In the end I left the works. In the mornings the time of the shift still wakes me, though the shift's long gone.
exact.лаборантка на химическом комбинате под Г: laboratory assistant at a chemical works near Halle
exact.После училища меня взяли лаборанткой на: After college they took me on as a lab assistant at the chemical works. We went to work by bus, all with the same bags, and at first I mixed mine up with other people's.
exact.Я научилась по запаху в цеху понимать, к: I learned to tell which shift was on by the smell in the shop. That skill was no use to me anywhere afterwards, but I was very proud of it.
exact.С комбината я ушла на пенсию. Белый хала: I retired from the chemical works. My white coat still hangs at home, I wear it to paint the windows.
exact.доярка в сельхозкооперативе (LPG) в Альт: milkmaid at an agricultural cooperative (LPG) in the Altmark
exact.Когда хозяйства объединили в кооператив,: When the farms were merged into a cooperative I went to the dairy as a milkmaid. The cows were the same ones the neighbours had before, only now they were shared, and I don't think they ever understood it.
exact.Со временем я стала старшей по ферме. Сп: In time I became head of the dairy. I learned to argue with the chairman politely, but so that he remembered.
exact.С фермы я ушла, когда руки стали болеть: I left the dairy when my hands started aching in the mornings. But I still get up before dawn, my body remembers milking better than I do.
exact.сдавала комнаты гостям Страстей в Оберам: let rooms to Passion Play visitors in Oberammergau
exact.Работа у меня была домашняя: в годы пред: My work was at home: in play years I let rooms to visitors, and in the other years I got the house ready for the next time. The first guests came when I still couldn't remember where we kept the spare pillows.
exact.Я научилась за один вечер понимать, кто: I learned to tell in one evening which guests would complain and which would leave a thank-you note. I was rarely wrong, and when I was, those were the best guests.
exact.Комнаты я сдавать перестала, когда лестн: I stopped letting rooms when the stairs got too steep for me. I keep the book the guests signed, there's handwriting from all over the world in it.
exact.После учительской семинарии меня послали: After teacher training college they sent me to a village school. Children of different ages sat in one room, and the little ones learned from the older ones faster than from me.
exact.Я знала все семьи в округе, кто чем боле: I knew every family around, who was ill and whose cow had calved again. At school it helped, at meetings it got in the way.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из сельской школы. Бывш: I retired from the village school. My old pupils still greet me first, and some of them, out of old habit, hide their hands behind their backs.
exact.Я была совсем маленькая в ту зиму, котор: I was very little the winter they later called the turnip winter. Mum said they ate turnip every way you could think of then, and I suppose I did too.
exact.Картошка в тот год не уродилась, и брюкв: The potatoes failed that year, and turnips were given out instead of everything. Turnip in the soup, turnip instead of potatoes, turnip for pudding, I thought even the washing smelt of it.
exact.Картошка в тот год не уродилась, и в дек: The potatoes failed that year, and in December all the turnips were requisitioned so there'd be something to feed people. That winter was called the turnip winter, and I haven't eaten a turnip since, not for anything.
exact.Потом ещё долго дома ничего не выбрасыва: For a long time afterwards nothing at home was thrown away, not even peelings.
exact.Мы стояли в очередях, а дома мама придум: We stood in queues, and at home Mum tried to make the turnip not taste like turnip. She never managed it once. It's funny, but I remember that grudge against a vegetable better than plenty of other things.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, кайзер от: When I was very little the Kaiser abdicated, a republic was declared, and two days later the war ended. I know that from what I was told.
exact.В ноябре вдруг сказали, что кайзера боль: In November they suddenly said there was no Kaiser any more and now it was a republic, and two days later the war ended. I kept asking where the Kaiser had gone, and nobody gave me a proper answer.
exact.Девятого ноября объявили, что кайзер отр: On the ninth of November they announced that the Kaiser had abdicated and proclaimed a republic, and on the eleventh the armistice was signed. The next day they also said women would vote now, and my friends and I didn't know what to be amazed at first.
exact.Слово «республика» сначала произносили о: At first people said the word "republic" carefully, like a stranger's name.
exact.Вокруг говорили про советы рабочих и сол: All around people talked about workers' and soldiers' councils, some were glad, some were afraid. What I remember more is that the war was finally over, and nobody knew what would come next.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, деньги дешевели: When I was little money lost its value so fast that you had to ask the price all over again every day. I know that from the grown-ups.
exact.В двадцать третьем за доллар давали снач: In twenty-three a dollar cost thousands of marks at first, then millions. Mum got her money and ran straight off to spend it while it was still worth something, and she took me with her so there'd be two of us running.
exact.В двадцать третьем марка падала так, что: In twenty-three the mark fell so fast that wages were spent the same day, by the next they weren't worth anything. Then in November they brought in the Rentenmark, one for a trillion of the old ones, and we spent a long time learning to count again.
exact.После этого деньги на чёрный день многие: After that a lot of people kept their rainy-day money in things, not in money.
exact.Сбережения, которые копили годами, раста: Savings put by for years melted in a few days. I remember a neighbour laughing that her dowry would now buy a box of matches, and it wasn't a cheerful laugh at all.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, работы не было у: When I was little millions of people had no work, and the banks were closing their counters. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Без работы тогда сидели миллионы, и мужч: Millions had no work then, and men stood about in our yard in the daytime with nothing to do, it seemed strange to me. Then in the summer the banks shut, and the grown-ups talked only about who'd managed to get their money out.
exact.Весной безработных было почти пять милли: In the spring there were nearly five million unemployed, and not all of them got benefit. In July a big bank collapsed, the counters were shut for two days, and people stood at the doors though they knew they wouldn't open.
People held on to a job as if it were the last one.
exact.Мы научились жить на очень мало и не гов: We learned to live on very little and not to say so out loud. Pride cost more than bread then, only it didn't put any more bread on the table.
exact.Про весну тридцать третьего я знаю тольк: About the spring of thirty-three I only know from what I was told: how they burned books in May and then cleared out of the libraries whatever had become forbidden. They told me quietly, and not straight away.
exact.В мае студенты жгли книги, а потом из би: In May students burned books, and then they started taking authors out of the libraries who weren't allowed any more. I didn't understand how a book could be guilty, and I no longer dared ask out loud.
exact.В мае тридцать третьего студенческий сою: In May thirty-three the students' union burned books by opposition and Jewish authors, and then the libraries were purged. Some were glad, some kept quiet, and keeping quiet soon became a habit.
exact.Дома стали думать, какие книги стоят на: At home people started thinking about which books stood on the shelf in plain sight.
exact.Я не стану рассказывать больше, чем виде: I won't tell more than I saw myself. I'll only say that people learned very quickly then what wasn't talked about, even children.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, началась: When I was very little the war began. I grew up with the blackout and ration cards as ordinary life, I didn't remember any other.
exact.Первого сентября Германия напала на Поль: On the first of September Germany attacked Poland, and two days later Britain and France declared war on it. The windows were blacked out, from the end of the month food was on ration cards, and I learned the cards before my times tables.

On the first of September Germany attacked Poland, on the third Britain and France declared war on it. There was a blackout, listening to foreign radio was banned, and from the end of September food, and then clothes as well, were on ration cards.
exact.Вечерами окна закрывали наглухо, и город: In the evenings windows were shut tight, and the city went dark.
exact.Про войну в каждой семье помнили своё и: Every family remembered its own war and didn't like to talk about it. I'll talk about the ordinary things: queues, ration cards, endless darning. The rest can stay with me.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, Германия капитул: When I was little Germany surrendered and the war in Europe ended. I know that from the grown-ups.
exact.В мае объявили, что Германия капитулиров: In May they announced that Germany had surrendered and the war in Europe was over. The grown-ups didn't know whether to be glad or afraid, and did both at once.
exact.В мае подписали безоговорочную капитуляц: In May the unconditional surrender was signed, and the war in Europe was over. There was more relief than joy, and nobody knew what tomorrow would bring.
exact.В наш город к тому времени уже вошли вой: By then Allied troops had already entered our town, and now they decided what was allowed and what wasn't.
exact.В июне власть взяли четыре державы, стра: In June the four powers took over, the country was divided into zones, and Berlin into sectors.
exact.Первые недели после войны я помню хуже,: I remember the first weeks after the war worse than I'd like, and maybe that's for the best. I remember everyone counting who'd come back, and the quiet at night seemed suspicious.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, в западных зонах: When I was little they brought in new money in the western zones, the Deutsche Mark. Afterwards the grown-ups divided life into before that day and after.
exact.В июне ввели новые деньги, немецкую марк: In June they brought in new money, the Deutsche Mark, and the old money suddenly became bits of paper. I thought the new notes smelt different, and I sniffed them until Mum took them off me.
exact.Двадцатого июня в западных зонах провели: On the twentieth of June the currency reform was carried out in the western zones and the Deutsche Mark came in. Yesterday's money stopped being money in a single day, and everyone counted what they had left.
exact.Цены и зарплаты пришлось выучить заново,: Prices and wages had to be learned all over again, and money meant something again.
exact.Помню, как держала первые новые бумажки: I remember holding the first new notes and being afraid to spend them, though that's what they were given for. Some said life had started again, others that it had only started again for people who had something besides money.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, в советской зоне: When I was little the Soviet zone had its own currency reform, three days after the western one. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Летом у нас поменяли деньги, через три д: In the summer our money was changed, three days after they brought in their own in the west. The grown-ups kept comparing whose was better, and I didn't understand how money could be different in one country.
exact.Двадцать третьего июня в советской зоне: On the twenty-third of June the Soviet zone carried out its own currency reform, three days after the western one. It was clear that now we had one money and they had another, and not just money.
exact.А осенью сорок девятого у нас образовали: And in the autumn of forty-nine the GDR was founded on our side, a separate state.
exact.Все тогда считали, сколько у кого поменя: Everyone counted then how much they'd get exchanged. And those with family in the west also thought about how they paid with different money now, and letters slowly became different, though the same people were writing them.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, в июне пятьдесят: When I was little, in June fifty-three, there were strikes all over the country, and Soviet troops put the uprising down. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Весной подняли нормы и цены, а в июне ст: In the spring work quotas and prices went up, and in June the builders in Berlin downed tools, and the strike spread all over the country. Then Soviet troops came, and for a long time the grown-ups stopped talking about it in front of children.
exact.Весной подняли нормы выработки и цены, а: In the spring work quotas and prices went up, and on the seventeenth of June the builders on the Stalinallee went on strike, and dozens of towns rose after them. Soviet troops and the People's Police put the uprising down, and a lot of people were detained.
exact.Повышение норм потом отменили, а про тот: The higher quotas were withdrawn later, and that day was only talked about among people you trusted.
exact.Кто был там, а кто только слышал, потом: Who'd been there and who'd only heard kept it to themselves afterwards. I'll say what I know for certain: after that, for a very long time, nobody spoke loudly on the stairs.
exact.Когда я была маленькая, границу с Западо: When I was little the border with the West was shut for good, first in Berlin, then everywhere. I know that from the grown-ups.
exact.В августе перекрыли границу в Берлине, а: In August the border in Berlin was closed, and three days later the one with the FRG too. The grown-ups listened to the radio very quietly, and the trip I'd been promised was never mentioned again.
exact.Тринадцатого августа перекрыли границу в: On the thirteenth of August the border in Berlin was closed off, and on the sixteenth the border with the FRG was shut for everyone living in the GDR. Lots of people had been leaving before that, and now it was clear you couldn't leave any more.
exact.Письма и посылки стали главной ниточкой: Letters and parcels became the main thread to the people left on the other side.
exact.Кто-то успел уехать раньше, кто-то остал: Some got away before, some stayed and didn't regret it, some regretted it all their lives. I won't argue about it, everyone has their own truth, and so do I.
exact.Осенью восемьдесят девятого открыли гран: In the autumn of eighty-nine the border between the two Germanys was opened. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Осенью вдруг открыли границу, и люди пое: In the autumn the border suddenly opened, and people went where they hadn't been allowed before. The grown-ups cried in front of the television, and I couldn't tell if it was from happiness or not.
exact.Вечером девятого ноября объявили новые п: On the evening of the ninth of November they announced new travel rules, and by midnight the first crossings had opened. Over the next two days millions of people from the GDR went across, and everyone was given welcome money.
exact.Слова «туда» и «оттуда» потихоньку стали: The words "over there" and "from over there" slowly began to mean something else.
exact.Это было так, будто открыли дверь в комн: It was as if someone had opened the door to a room nobody had looked into for ages. People were glad, people cried, and the next morning lots of them went to work all the same, life wants what it wants.
exact.Летом девяностого у нас вместо наших ден: In the summer of ninety the western mark replaced our money. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Летом наши деньги поменяли на западную м: In the summer our money was changed for the western mark, and everything in the shops was different. The grown-ups counted and counted again, and I was pleased with the new coins.
exact.Первого июля немецкая марка стала нашими: On the first of July the Deutsche Mark became our only money. Wages and pensions were converted one to one, savings up to a certain amount too, and above it two to one, and prices were freed straight away.
exact.Цены пришлось узнавать заново, а за квар: We had to learn the prices all over again, and pay for the flat and the fares in a new way.
exact.Сначала все радовались западным деньгам,: At first everyone was glad of the western money, and then they started adding up the rent. I kept the old coins for a long time in a coffee tin, just in case, as if they might come back.
exact.Осенью девяностого Германия снова стала: In the autumn of ninety Germany became one country again. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Осенью объявили, что Германия теперь одн: In the autumn they announced that Germany was one now. The grown-ups talked about it so much that I stopped listening.
exact.Третьего октября ГДР присоединилась к ФР: On the third of October the GDR joined the FRG, and Germany became one country again. In December there were the first all-German elections since thirty-two.
exact.Привыкать к одной стране пришлось дольше: Getting used to one country took longer than announcing it.
exact.Одни говорили «наконец», другие «посмотр: Some said "at last", others "we'll see", and often they were the same people on different days. I said both myself.
exact.В две тысячи втором вместо немецкой марк: In two thousand and two the euro came in instead of the Deutsche Mark. I know that from what I was told.
exact.В две тысячи втором марку сменили на евр: In two thousand and two the mark was replaced by the euro, and the coins were quite different. I laid them out on the table like toy money.
exact.Первого января две тысячи второго вместо: On the first of January two thousand and two euro coins and notes came in instead of the Deutsche Mark. For years I kept converting prices into marks and gasping every time.
exact.Цены я ещё долго считала в уме в двух де: For a long time I worked out prices in my head in two currencies at once.
exact.Марку было жалко, хоть это и смешно, жал: I missed the mark, though it's funny to miss money rather than what you buy with it. I didn't take the last coins to the bank straight away, I held them in my hand for a bit first.
exact.Весной двадцатого всех попросили сидеть: In the spring of twenty twenty everyone was asked to stay at home because of the illness. I know that from what I was told.
exact.Весной двадцатого из-за болезни просили: In the spring of twenty twenty people were asked not to meet anyone because of the illness, and cafés and hairdressers closed. Everyone sat at home together and got in each other's way.
exact.В конце марта двадцатого договорились св: At the end of March twenty twenty they agreed to keep meetings to a minimum, keep a metre and a half apart and only go out alone or with family. The hairdressers shut, and to be honest that's what got to me most.
The phone calls got longer and the walks shorter.
exact.Я, если честно, переносила это лучше мно: To be honest I coped better than plenty of young people: I know how to stay at home. The only hard thing was not being able to hug anyone, and you can't do that over the phone.
exact.Летом западные секторы отрезали от дорог: In the summer the western sectors were cut off from the roads and waterways, and an airlift was started. The planes came over the city one after another, and in Berlin back then you could tell the time by their drone, wherever you lived.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в сорок вось: I was told later how in forty-eight the western sectors of Berlin were supplied by air.
exact.Под Эльбой открыли тоннель, и до верфей: They opened a tunnel under the Elbe, and you could walk to the shipyards on the other bank under the water. The first time I went through it I kept listening for drips from above.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как в Гамбурге открыли: I was told how in Hamburg they opened the tunnel under the Elbe and whole families went to look at it.
exact.В феврале сорок девятого впервые после в: In February forty-nine the Rose Monday parade went through for the first time since the war. The city was still in ruins, and people came out into the street all the same, and that seemed both strange and right to me.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Кёльне в п: I was told later how in Cologne the carnival parade went through again for the first time after the war.
exact.Летом в Мюнхене прошла Олимпиада, город: In the summer Munich held the Olympics, the city was full of visitors and talk in every language. And then came the attack on the Israeli team, and the celebration ended nothing like the way it began.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали про мюнхенскую Ол: I was told later about the Munich Olympics of seventy-two, both the cheerful part and the terrible one.
exact.Осенью по понедельникам люди выходили на: In the autumn people went out into the streets on Mondays after the prayers in St Nicholas Church. On the ninth of October there were more than seventy thousand of them, and everyone was afraid, and they went all the same.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали про понедельничны: I was told later about the Monday demonstrations in Leipzig in the autumn of eighty-nine.
exact.В пятидесятом Страсти поставили снова, в: In fifty the Passion Play was staged again, for the first time after the war, with the old text. People in America asked for it to be cancelled, and in the village they argued about that less than about who was playing whom.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как в Обераммергау в п: I was told how in fifty Oberammergau played the Passion again, the first time after the war.
exact.Новый город у комбината весной назвали С: In the spring the new town by the steelworks was named Stalinstadt. I got muddled for a long time over how to write the return address, and I think the postman got muddled even longer.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как новый город при ко: I was told how the new town by the steelworks was named Stalinstadt.
exact.Решили строить город для химиков, и чере: They decided to build a town for the chemical workers, and a couple of years later the first tenants moved in. People waited for a flat there the way they used to wait only for letters.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как под Галле строили: I was told how they built a new town for the chemical workers near Halle.
exact.В Альтмарке начали добывать газ, и в пол: In the Altmark they began extracting gas, and rigs and strange vehicles appeared in the fields. At first people went to look at them, and then stopped noticing.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как в Альтмарке нашли: I was told how gas was found in the Altmark and they began extracting it.
exact.В Вольфсбурге собрали миллионного «жука»: In Wolfsburg they built the millionth Beetle. The town talked about it as if each of them had built it personally.
exact.Мне рассказывали, как в Вольфсбурге собр: I was told how in Wolfsburg they built the millionth Beetle.
